AlternateTargets: take the slave for the gentleman
Senses.Note: The graph “gentleman/master” (郎) is rendered “master” here because the fixed contrast is household rank, not because the graph universally means a household master. The passages do not support separate senses for each object criticized.

SearchAliases: mistake the servant for the household head
take the slave for the gentleman
Zen mistake the servant for the household head
Senses.Explanation: Masters use the household reversal as an adverse appraisal in public exchanges and comments. It is repeatedly coupled with “point to a deer as a horse” (指鹿為馬). One address applies both verdicts even to the old advice “seek only from yourself, do not look elsewhere” (但向己求，莫從他覓); another identifies “taking the one capable of seeing and hearing as real” (認著一箇能見能聞……執以為真) as precisely mistaking servant for master. Elsewhere Xiangyan Yiduan permits bowing but warns, “you must not mistake the servant for the household head” (不得認奴作郎), while later case commentary applies the same verdict to Deshan. The ordinary status reversal becomes a portable Chan verdict on a proposed identification; which identification receives it is supplied by each passage.
